description: For the first time, a painting represented nothing at all from the visible world. **Kandinsky** set forms free; **Mondrian** cut everything down to geometry.

hero.hook: What if a painting no longer needed to describe the world in order to move you?

blocks.text: In the **1910s** and **1920s**, abstraction broke the oldest rule in painting: [[mimesis]], the duty to represent the visible world. A painting is no longer a window; it is an object in its own right.
Two parallel quests: **Wassily Kandinsky** translated the soul into free forms, while **Piet Mondrian** looked for the laws of the universe in pure geometry.

**Wassily Kandinsky** (1866-1944), a Russian lawyer turned painter, settled in Munich. Around **1910**, coming home at dusk, he was struck by a canvas whose subject he could not make out. It was one of his own, standing upside down. From then on, resemblance to the real world looked to him like an obstacle.

blocks.caption: Around 1910, Kandinsky took the step into abstraction

blocks.text: A synesthete, he said he could “hear” colors and “see” sounds. Hence his titles: Compositions, Improvisations.

In **1911**, he published *Concerning the Spiritual in Art* and set out the theory of [[lyrical abstraction]]. Every color has its vibration: blue suggests the heavenly, while yellow, harsher, can “sound” like a trumpet. Painting should work on the soul the way music does, with no story.

sections.title: Kandinsky: painting the way you compose music

blocks.text: The Dutchman **Piet Mondrian** (1872-1944) reached abstraction through a slow [[decantation]] of the real world. Between **1908** and **1912**, his tree series show trunk and branches dissolving into a grid of lines.

blocks.caption: From tree to network of lines: Mondrian simplifies down to the essential

blocks.text: In restaurants he often asked to sit with his back to the window, so he would not have to see trees and gardens he found too disorderly.

In **1917**, he founded the **De Stijl** movement and set out **Neoplasticism**: reduce art to the elements of the cosmos. Only the straight line and the three primary colors remain. The right angle was meant to express the balance of universal forces, far from individual emotion. He even banned green from his studio as too “natural.”

Abstraction did not stay in the museum. At the [[Bauhaus]], the school of architecture and applied arts founded by [[Walter Gropius]] in **1919**, painters, architects, and designers worked side by side. Kandinsky taught there, and Mondrian's aesthetic fed into floor plans and facades.

blocks.caption: The Bauhaus: when abstract art meets design and architecture

blocks.text: At the Bauhaus, Kandinsky had his students match shapes to colors. His conclusion: yellow triangle, red square, blue circle.
Modern design was born: “form follows function.” Gerrit Rietveld's famous Red and Blue Chair looks like a Mondrian in 3D. Mondrian himself thought that a real object broke the purity of abstraction.

sections.title: The Bauhaus: abstraction in daily life

blocks.text: With no story to tell, the painting invites the viewer to project a meaning onto it. That freedom opened the door to [[Conceptual Art]], where the idea matters more than the material. After the wars, abstraction also said what figurative painting could no longer carry.

events.detail: Concerning the Spiritual in Art set out lyrical abstraction.
events.title: Kandinsky turns abstract

events.detail: Mondrian reduced art to lines and primary colors.
events.title: De Stijl

blocks.text: From our smartphone interfaces to street signs, their lesson holds. American [[Abstract Expressionism]] and [[Minimal Art]] carried the revolution further.
Abstract art came from two paths: Kandinsky freed form to speak of the soul; Mondrian turned the world into geometry to reach the universal.
